s1.quote: sunk at a depth of approximately 97 feet (30 m)

s2.quote: Since the Carthaginian lays at 100 feet, you need to hold an advanced certification for this charter.

summary.text: A scuttled replica whaling ship lying upright on sand off Lahaina, Maui, about half a mile offshore. Deep enough that operators ask for advanced certification; it is a popular artificial reef wreck.

sites.name: Major General Wallace F. Randolph

s1.quote: The wreck sits on a flat sandy bottom 120 feet (37 m) below the surface of the water

s2.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s2.quote: now lies intact and upright on a sand bottom in 120 feet of water

highlights.text: Intact upright hull with cable reel on the bow

summary.text: The Thunderbolt, a former Army minelayer sunk as an artificial reef about four miles off Marathon in the Florida Keys. It sits upright and intact on sand and offers penetration, but depth and current make it an advanced dive.

sites.depthNote: Cable reel at 80 ft, superstructure 75 ft, props at 120 ft

s1.publisher: National Park Service, Biscayne National Park
s1.quote: The wreck of Arratoon Apcar lies in ten to twenty feet of water near Fowey Rocks. … The coral-encrusted lower hull and iron beams of the vessel can still be seen

s2.quote: The wreck is at a depth of 10 to 20 feet (3 to 6 m) near Fowey Rocks.

summary.text: The remains of an 1878 iron steamer in shallow water on Fowey Rocks in Biscayne National Park, part of the park's wreck trail. Coral-covered hull ribs and lots of fish make it good for snorkelers and divers.

s1.quote: She currently rests upright in 97 feet (30 m).

s2.quote: The wreckage is twisted in two pieces with large gaping holes … Penetration is tricky, watch out for entanglement … Advanced Open Water or equivalent experience

summary.text: A freighter scuttled in 1985 off Fort Lauderdale as an artificial reef. It lies broken in two pieces with gaping holes in about 97 feet; divers need Advanced certification and care with entanglement.

s1.quote: She sits in 25 feet of water

s2.quote: lies in just twenty five feet of clear, warm water, on the east edge of Looe reef

highlights.text: Iron ballast stack and scattered artifacts of 1744 frigate

summary.text: The remains of an 18th-century British frigate lost in 1744 on the eastern edge of Looe Key reef off Big Pine Key. Shallow, clear water and the stacked iron ballast make it an easy historic wreck dive.

s1.quote: only twenty feet of gloriously clear water … the park service has no plans to open these wrecks up to the public

access.value: Wreck site not open to the public (National Park archaeological site)

s1.quote: The San Jose sank in twenty-eight-foot waters
The depth ranges from 7 feet to 30 feet. … a spur-and-groove reef with coral fingers that extend out to sea, separated by white-sand channels

s2.quote: Max Depth: 30 ft. … the depth ranges from 7 feet to 30 feet

s3.publisher: NOAA Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary
s3.quote: located approximately 6.3 miles south of Ramrod Key … a classic spur and groove coral formation

access.value: Sanctuary Preservation Area with special regulations; boat only

summary.text: A spur-and-groove coral reef about six miles offshore of Ramrod and Big Pine Keys, protected as a sanctuary preservation area. Shallow coral fingers and sand channels hold reef sharks, rays and groupers.

s2.quote: Barrel-shaped coral heads, spur-and-groove formation. Easy navigation, healthy coral, stingrays and juvenile nurse sharks in the sand channels. … 10–25 ft

highlights.text: Juvenile nurse sharks and stingrays in sand channels
Remains of the Pickle Barrel civil-war era wreck

summary.text: A shallow spur-and-groove reef off Key Largo with barrel-shaped coral heads, easy navigation and sea fans. Gentle depths suit new divers and snorkelers, and small fish make it a good photo site.

sites.name: S.S. Sapona

s1.quote: The wreck sits in 15 feet of water, just a few miles off Bennett's Harbour in South Bimini

s2.quote: 15-30 feet (5-9 meters) … Currents are generally mild … Beginner to Intermediate

highlights.text: Concrete ship partly above water with swim-throughs

summary.text: A WWI-era concrete freighter aground in shallow water off South Bimini, Bahamas (not the US). Holes from WWII bombing practice let light into swim-throughs, making it easy for snorkelers and new divers.

sites.depthNote: Pin is in the Bahamas (Bimini), not the United States

s1.quote: It rests in 15-20 feet of water, with wreckage rising as much as six feet off the sea floor depending on sand movement. … anchor in the sand

access.value: Florida Underwater Archaeological Preserve, open free year-round; anchor in sand

hazards.text: Sand movement buries or exposes parts of the wreck

summary.text: An 1898 iron barque wrecked and later blasted, leaving a scattered wreck site just off Manalapan near Boynton Beach in about 15 to 20 feet. It is a state archaeological preserve suited to snorkelers and new divers.

s1.quote: 80 Feet … during flood tide, as an outgoing tide will pull murky water from the inlet … Advanced Divers

s2.quote: Sunk in 85 feet (26 m) of water … advanced dive site

hazards.text: Murky inlet water on outgoing tide

summary.text: A cargo ship scuttled in 1968 off Riviera Beach near Palm Beach Inlet. Only the hull and lower deck remain; strong currents and tide-dependent visibility make it an advanced dive best done on a flood tide.

s1.quote: depths to 32 feet … an easy beginner to intermediate shore dive site … Currents can be running along shore from north or south, making for a great drift dive.

s2.quote: With depths of upto 30 feet, you have plenty to explore along the underwater rocky ledge

highlights.text: Green sea turtles and night-time eels, lobsters, reef squid

summary.text: Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) at Ka'anapali is an easy beach-entry dive along a rocky ledge reaching about 30 feet. Suited to beginners, with turtles by day and octopus, eels and squid at night.

s1.quote: She had sunk in just 12 to 18 feet (3.7 to 5.5 m) of water

sites.name: Manta Ray Heaven, Garden Eel Cove

s1.quote: Manta Heaven has a slightly wider depth range, from 20 to 50 feet, but most of the action happens at an average depth of around 35 feet.

s2.quote: The reef starts at about 20' and gently slopes 50-100 yards to 40' where the drop off starts.

s3.quote: Garden Eel Cove (northern Airport site) … 80 to 100 feet of visibility not uncommon

highlights.text: Night manta ray feeding under dive lights
Garden eels on the sandy bottom

hazards.text: Exposed to open ocean; boat ride can be choppy

summary.text: A coral shelf in Makako Bay off Kona airport that is a day site for garden eels and, at night, the Big Island's manta ray dive. Operators run boat trips; divers kneel on sand at about 35 feet while mantas feed on plankton.

s1.quote: An Easy beginner to intermediate site … depths to 45 feet on the outer reaches … Very protected bay, so diving is good here even when others are not

highlights.text: Protected C-shaped bay, good night diving

s1.quote: Maximum Depth: 40 feet … Beginner … If Sound swells are running - vis will be poor.

s2.quote: mellow waters and gradual incline … great turtle cleaning station on the second reef

highlights.text: Turtle cleaning station on the second reef

hazards.text: Poor visibility when swells are running

summary.text: A beach-entry reef dive in Wailea, South Maui, used for scuba instruction thanks to gentle conditions and a gradual slope. Turtles visit a cleaning station on the second reef; swells can ruin visibility.
